author: grand canyon times
title: Ciscomani announces new mission for Fort Huachuca in Arizona's 6th District - Grand Canyon Times
text:
Congressman Juan Ciscomani announced on Apr. 15 that the U.S. Department of War has chosen Fort Huachuca as the location for a new military mission.
The selection of Fort Huachuca is seen as significant for Sierra Vista, Cochise County, and Arizona, with implications for national security and local employment. Ciscomani said, “This new mission is a win for Sierra Vista and Cochise County, a win for Arizona and a win for our national security.” He added that the decision reflects Fort Huachuca’s importance as “an unequalled strategic asset, not just today, but for the future of our national defense.”
Ciscomani has advocated since last year to bring this mission to Arizona’s 6th Congressional District by working with the Trump Administration and Secretary of the Air Force. He highlighted Fort Huachuca’s long history: “Fort Huachuca got its start in the 19th century as a frontier cavalry garrison,” he said. “The Fort that was once the home of the legendary Buffalo Soldiers is now the tip of the spear for some of the most technologically advanced 21st century military missions, including the U.S. Army Intelligence Center of Excellence, the Network Enterprise Technology Command and the Electronic Proving Ground.”
Fort Huachuca is located about 15 miles north of Mexico’s border and serves as Cochise County’s largest employer. The base covers nearly one thousand square miles of restricted airspace along with over two thousand square miles dedicated to electronic ranges.
Ciscomani also pointed out regional strengths: “The case for the Fort was strengthened,” he said, “by a regional ecosystem that includes the University of Arizona, Raytheon, Northrop Grumman and Honeywell. Fort Huachuca’s one-of-a-kind capabilities, its location and supporting infrastructure made it an obvious choice for this new mission. We should all be proud of this major win.” Ciscomani has represented Arizona’s 6th district in Congress since replacing Ann Kirkpatrick in 2023 according to election results.
He won his seat after defeating Kirsten Engel in both 2022—by roughly one percent—and again in 2024 as reported by election data. Born in Hermosillo, Mexico in 1982 and currently living in Tucson according to congressional records, Ciscomani graduated from University of Arizona with a Bachelor’s degree in 2005.
